record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: For a dispersive billiard table Y, let f_Y(n) denote the number of periodic orbits of the billiard map whose period is at most n. Does the exponential growth rate h = lim_{n→∞} (log f_Y(n))/n exist?

evidence.quote: Let fY (n) be the number of periodic orbits, whose period is less than or equal to n.
Problem 5. Does the limit below exist? h = limn→∞ log fY (n) / n (2.2)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Y \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a dispersive (Sinai) billiard table: a compact domain whose boundary consists of finitely many smooth strictly convex arcs whose curvature, viewed from inside $Y$, is negative (i.e., the boundary is convex into the table). Consider the associated billiard map $T_Y$ defined on the unit tangent bundle restricted to the boundary, where a point particle moves in straight lines inside $Y$ and reflects elastically off the boundary. For each integer $n \geq 1$, let $f_Y(n)$ denote the number of periodic orbits of $T_Y$ whose period (number of collisions in one cycle) is at most $n$.

Determine whether the limit
$$h \;=\; \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{\log f_Y(n)}{n}$$
exists for every dispersive billiard table $Y$.
artifact.status_search_result: Existing results (Burago–Ferleger, Stoyanov, and others) establish exponential upper bounds on the number of periodic orbits for semi-dispersing billiards and finiteness of topological entropy, but the existence of the actual limit (as opposed to limsup) of (log f_Y(n))/n for dispersive billiards does not appear to have been established in the literature. The problem is listed as an open problem in surveys of billiard dynamics.

status_evidence.title: An estimate from above of the number of periodic orbits for semi-dispersed billiards
status_evidence.snippet: For a large class of semi-dispersed billiards an exponential estimate from above is found for the number of periodic points of the billiard ball map.
status_evidence.claim: Only an exponential upper bound (limsup) is known; existence of the limit is not established.

status_evidence.title: The growth rate for the number of singular and periodic orbits for a polygonal billiard
status_evidence.snippet: Growth rate results for periodic orbits in billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses growth rates but does not settle the dispersive case limit existence.
